source_text: Recederet postremo post donum gratiae coeuntium pudor nec iret per membra quietis imitatio nec paterentur sensus onera dulcedinis, liberum postremo baptizatis redderetur arbitrium, ut per correctionem naturae expulsa lege peccati tam possibile confitereris esse mortalibus nitere splendore virtutum quam sordibus horrere vitiorum, immo penitus nec mortales, qui sacramentis imbuuntur, esse deberent.
pass_a_gloss: Finally after the gift of grace the modesty of those coupling would recede, nor would an imitation of rest go through the members, nor would the senses suffer the burdens of sweetness; finally free decision would be rendered to the baptized, so that, through a correction of nature, the law of sin having been expelled, you would confess it as possible for mortals to shine with the splendor of virtues as to bristle with the filths of vices, nay inwardly those who are imbued with the sacraments ought not even to be mortal.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS donum; Blaise grace-gift vs inherited sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: After the gift of grace, the modesty of those coupling should disappear; no semblance of repose should spread through their limbs; their senses should not undergo the burden of sweetness. Finally, free will should be restored to the baptized, so that, with nature corrected and the law of sin expelled, you would acknowledge that mortals can as readily shine with the brilliance of virtues as be repulsive with the filth of vices. Indeed, those initiated into the sacraments should not be mortal at all.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Rom 5 contrast of Adam's offense and Christ's gift; keep gift, not later 'grace system'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: “Semblance of repose” translates quietis imitatio literally; the precise physiological sensation meant in this description of sexual response is uncertain.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
